notice: RN bank batch 145: Pediatric neurologic case studies: shunt malfunction, febrile seizure, myelomeningocele and abusive head trauma. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the 1-hour findings that require immediate action.

rationale.correct: Cushing triad with falling consciousness means shunt failure with rising ICP.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each sign, indicate whether it is an early or late sign of raised ICP in children.

rows.text: Headache and vomiting, especially in the morning
Irritability and poor feeding
Bulging fontanel in an infant
Bradycardia with irregular breathing
Fixed dilated pupil

rationale.correct: Cushing triad and pupil changes are late.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse should {{b1}}, and the child is likely to need {{b2}}.

options.text: raise the head of the bed and call the neurosurgeon now
lay the child flat with legs raised
give oral fluids for the vomiting

rationale.correct: Head up and neurosurgery.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: After shunt revision, which parts of the plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Position as ordered, often flat at first to avoid overdrainage
Watch the incision and tract for redness or fluid
Pump the shunt to test it every hour
Lay the child on the shunt side

rationale.correct: Positioning, neuro checks, site and temperature.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: The nurse gives handoff to the PICU nurse. Which information is most important? Select all that apply.

options.text: The parents' insurance details and billing contact
A list of the child's favorite foods only

rationale.correct: Baseline, surgery details, trends and parent-observed signs.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.educationalObjective: Take action with an effective handoff.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement by the parent, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "Vomiting without diarrhea, headache or sleepiness means I call right away."
"Fever or redness along the tubing means infection."
"The shunt will need to be checked as my child grows."
"I'll pump the shunt every morning to keep it working."
"My child can't ever play outside."

rationale.correct: Know the signs; normal activity with limits.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that need immediate action during the second seizure.

rationale.correct: A seizure over 5 minutes needs rescue medicine.

questions.stem: For each feature, indicate whether it fits a simple or complex febrile seizure.

rows.text: Generalized, less than 15 minutes
Focal features
More than one in 24 hours
Age 6 months to 5 years with fever
Longer than 15 minutes

rationale.correct: Simple seizures are brief, generalized and single.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: Without IV access, the first rescue medicine is {{b1}}, and if seizures continue, {{b2}} is next.

options.text: a second benzodiazepine dose, then levetiracetam or fosphenytoin IV/IO

rationale.correct: Benzodiazepine first, then a second-line drug.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Intranasal midazolam 0.2 mg/kg is prescribed. The toddler weighs 12 kg. The concentration is 5 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give? Record your answer to two decimal places.

rationale.correct: 0.2 x 12 = 2.4 mg; 2.4 / 5 = 0.48 mL, split between the nostrils.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Midazolam 0.2 mg/kg intranasal now. Oxygen. IO access if no IV.

questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse take during the seizure? Select all that apply.

options.text: Turn the child on the side
Put a finger in the mouth to stop tongue biting
Hold the arms and legs still

rationale.correct: Side-lying, oxygen, timing and safety.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement by the parent, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll give the nasal midazolam if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, then call 911."
"Fever medicine helps comfort but doesn't prevent febrile seizures."
"Most children grow out of febrile seizures."
"I'll put my child in a cold bath during a fever."
"I'll give aspirin for the fever."

rationale.correct: Rescue plan; no cold baths or aspirin.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

caseStudies.title: VP shunt malfunction in a toddler

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 2-year-old child with a VP shunt for hydrocephalus has vomited four times since waking without diarrhea. The parent says the child is "not acting right" and keeps holding the head.

caseStudies.title: Febrile seizure progressing to status epilepticus

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 20-month-old toddler with an ear infection had a 2-minute generalized seizure at home with a fever of 39.6 C. The toddler is now sleepy but rousable. Fifteen minutes after arrival, the toddler has another seizure.

exhibits.title: NICU, 2 hours old
exhibits.body: A term newborn has a lumbar myelomeningocele found on prenatal ultrasound. The sac is intact. Surgery is planned within 48 hours.

caseStudies.title: Abusive head trauma in an infant

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 4-month-old infant is brought by the parent's partner, who says the infant "rolled off the couch" onto a carpet. The infant is not feeding and is very sleepy. The infant cannot yet roll over, according to the clinic chart.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
